svg.text: Our testbed · Bowling Green / Warren County, KY
Mapping floods in Bowling Green from space: what we are doing
Phases 0 and 1 of the testbed · all numbers are our real results (2016–2025 data)
Big idea:
Satellites show water now and then; river gauges show it every 15 minutes. Use each to fix the other.
The question

g.text: Barren River · Drakes Creek · Bowling Green
where? how deep? on which days?

svg.text: Where does Bowling Green flood, and how deep, on many
days and in fine detail? Water comes from the rivers
and from karst sinkholes.
The ingredients

g.text: radar sees through cloud, day and night

svg.text: Radar satellites see through cloud. Sentinel-1 imaged
the county on 571 dates since 2016, NISAR on 58 since
Oct 2025. No ICEYE or Umbra scene covers it yet.
Phase 0: which floods were seen?
Gauges and news reports give 51 flood events since
2016; 46 were imaged by at least one satellite. The
biggest: Feb and Apr 2025.
Phase 1: dark on radar = water

g.text: image only: ≈ 650 km² 'water', half the county ✗

svg.text: Calm water reflects the radar away, so it looks dark.
The hard part is the cut-off. Chosen from the image
alone it fails here: the county has too little water to
learn from.
Let the gauge choose the cut-off

g.text: to the river, should be wet

svg.text: The gauge's water level plus the elevation map say
where water must be; we keep the cut-off that matches
best. Our 17 Feb map agrees closely with NASA's OPERA
map.
Where it goes next

g.text: All on one 10 m grid + confidence
weight each sensor by its measured accuracy
fills the days between satellite passes

svg.text: Flood-only calibration gives -14.0 dB (Barren) and
-12.5 dB (Drakes), but from only 2–3 passes. More flood
events, NISAR and ICEYE come next.
Data: NASA/ESA Sentinel-1 (OPERA RTC, DSWx-S1), NASA-ISRO NISAR, USGS gauges and 3DEP, JRC water, Groundsource (Google Research). Schematic illustration.
